goal: Martin, 2026-09-03: *"Många steps tar lång tid, jag vill att vi ökar upp antalet parallella steps som kan göras från 2 till 4."* — and, the same day, when told the two lanes shared one round: *"Varje lane måste naturligtvis köra separat."* And a verb to set the count with: *"t ex 'mc step' 'Välj antalet parallella steps.'"*

**Measured before anything moved** (`measurements.md`, 2026-09-03, 60 sessions): a step's time is the session's own turns and test reruns. Median 19 min, 76 turns; 5 598 Bash calls against 255 native tool calls, 2 803 of them `sed -n`/`grep -n` reads of a screen at a time; 11 test-class commands per session, one in four an exact repeat; 15 % of tool time in `sleep` loops polling a backgrounded suite. Landing a step is a median 0.9 min and the runner's own overhead is one second. And the lanes stood idle 43–56 % of the time — blocked plans, a schema migration the runner's checkout had not caught up with, dirty worktrees skipped 134 rounds in a row, and a round that ended only when both lanes had.

So the order is: fewer turns and one test run per step, each lane on its own clock, the gate lock waiting instead of refusing — then the measurement against the numbers above, and only then a lane count above one.

There is no 2 to raise today. `splitLanes` (`src/mc/run.js`) returns one lane per repository and `runLane` walks its names one step at a time; two repositories with ready plans is two lanes. Reaching four means several steps at once **inside** one repository, and `gate-lock.js` — one gate round at a time on this machine, refusing rather than queueing (Martin, 2026-08-30: *"En instans kan köra åt gången."*) — stands in the way of that.
contract: **The gate stays serial.** Whatever the lane count becomes, one gate round at a time on this machine is not up for negotiation — the flakiness it absorbs is the 55 → 57 → 55 the red floor exists for. What may change is that a second round **waits** instead of being refused, so a wider lane count cannot throw away finished work.

**Step 4 reads step 3 before it builds.** The steps are an order — lock, measurement, count — and a step-4 session that finds the measurement says the count is not the bottleneck stops and blocks itself rather than building it. Martin, 2026-09-03, on the window that gated this: *"20 är bara taget ur luften. Det tar för lång tid allt. Slå på projekten nu."*

**mc is symlinked into its own working tree.** `/opt/homebrew/bin/mc` resolves to `/Users/martinforsberg/memoro-cli/src/mc-cli.js`. A change to how the runner or a session behaves lands through the gate and reaches the running runner by `mc run --update` (or STOP and start) — nobody edits `~/memoro-cli` by hand, and no step of this project edits `src/` in that checkout.
**Nothing changes what a step session may write.** The trespass check in `run.js` and the four fields a step owns (`status`, `pr`, `comments`, `met`) are not this project's to loosen.
**One step, one PR.** `mc` prints the page and `mc run --rounds 1` completes a round after each. A step that cannot keep both working stops and says so. No force-push, no rewritten history.
out_of_scope: **What a step session verifies beyond its `done_when`.** Step 1 tells the role to run the selection once and to leave screenshots and dev servers to a `done_when` that asks for them; rewriting individual plans' `done_when` is those plans' business.
**Adding repositories.** More lanes by adding a third repository is not what was asked for and is not a runner change.
**`budget_minutes`.** Two of fifteen rounds on 2026-09-02 died on their budget (exit 143, `no-json`). Whether the budget is right is a real question and not this one.
**Cloud or remote execution.** The lanes are inside the one local `mc run` process and stay there.
**The 18 plans parked on `plan-review`** (step 0's audit). That is Martin's reading queue; no mechanism here flips a `decision` blocker.

success_criteria.criterion: Every blocked step on origin/main in both repositories has been read, and each one either still has a live reason to be blocked or has been turned back to ready — with the count of each stated. Today that is 28 blocked against 4 ready in memoro.
success_criteria.check: A table in `docs/project/mc/step-parallelism/blocked-audit.md` naming every blocked step, what its `blocked_by` says, whether that thing is still true on main, and the disposition. The re-count after the sweep is run with the same script, checked in beside it.

success_criteria.criterion: A blocked step whose blocker has finished is surfaced without a person having to notice it — mc says so on its own.
success_criteria.check: With a plan blocked on a project whose plan is `done` on main, the surface named in step 1's design (a `mc status`/page line, or a runner.log line, whichever that step settles on) reports it; driven by a test with a real fixture pair rather than by inspection.

success_criteria.criterion: It is written down, with measured numbers rather than reasoning, how a step's wall-clock time divides between the headless session, the gate round, and the git and GitHub work around them — for at least 20 rounds.
success_criteria.check: `docs/project/mc/step-parallelism/measurements.md`, produced by `measure.py` beside it from `~/mc/runner/log/` and the session transcripts, with the row count stated. 60 sessions, 2026-09-01..03.

success_criteria.criterion: The number of gate-lock refusals under today's two lanes is counted, not estimated — the figure that says whether raising the lane count would throw work away.
success_criteria.check: `measurements.md` § *The runner and the gate*: 9 refusals in `gate-rounds.jsonl` in total, 0 since 2026-09-02.

success_criteria.criterion: A step session under the launch step 1 lands uses fewer turns and fewer test runs than the baseline: median turns and test-class commands per session, over the step sessions since the change, against 76 turns and 11 test commands.
success_criteria.check: `measure.py --since <landing day>` in `measurements.md` § *After* (step 3), with the session count stated. A drop of less than a quarter in either number is reported as such, not rounded up to a win.

success_criteria.check: A test drives two rounds against one lock without either losing work; `gate-rounds.jsonl` after the change carries no `another gate round is running` reason.

documents.label: The proposal this came from — `mc run` follows one project to the end

steps.title: Read every blocked step, free the ones whose blocker is gone, and make mc say it next time
steps.done_when: `docs/project/mc/step-parallelism/blocked-audit.md` accounts for every blocked step on origin/main in both repositories — blocker, whether it still holds, disposition — the ones whose blocker has finished are back to `ready` on main, and mc reports a stale blocker on its own rather than waiting to be noticed.
instruction: **The fault, in Martin's words on 2026-09-03:** *"vi måste förbättra hur ready sätts då planer kan stoppas utan avsikt"*. A step is `blocked` with `blocked_by: { kind, name }` — `kind` is `decision` or `project` (`BLOCKER_KINDS`, `src/mc/plan-schema.js`). Nothing in mc ever re-reads that name to ask whether it is still true. The runner hands out `ready` steps and reads nothing else, so a step whose blocker finished months ago is invisible to it for ever. A blocker does not flip itself.

**The size of it, measured 2026-09-03 on origin/main.** memoro: **28 blocked, 4 ready**. memoro-cli: 0 blocked, 2 ready. Four of memoro's twenty-eight are not a queue — they are the queue, and the other twenty-eight are parked. How many are parked *wrongly* is exactly what this step finds out; the number is not known yet and must not be guessed at in the PR.

**The one confirmed case, and the cost of clearing it by hand.** `email-window-layout` step 5 (the actions button in the reader header) was blocked on `action-window`. `action-window` was done; the blocker was satisfied in substance and nobody had flipped it. Clearing it took a person noticing, an edit to the plan, a docs-only pull request (#11277, landed as `5a36b80` through `mc merge --docs`), and putting the name back in `~/mc/queue.md`. That is the manual path this step is meant to make unnecessary — for the *noticing*, at least.

**Do the sweep by reading, not by a rule.** Take every `blocked` step on `origin/main` in both repositories. For each, write down what `blocked_by` names, and then go and look: for `kind: project`, whether that project's plan on main is `done` or gone; for `kind: decision`, whether the answer exists anywhere. Put all of it in `blocked-audit.md` with the disposition per row. A step whose blocker you cannot account for stays blocked and says so — the same discipline the `i18n-orphan-keys` proposal uses for a namespace nobody can explain.

**Flip only what the audit earned, and land it the cheap way.** Setting a step back to `ready` is a plan edit, which is documentation: `mc merge <repo> <pr> --docs` lands it without a gate round, and it is refused if anything outside `docs/` is in the diff. Group them so a reader can check the reasoning — one PR per repository is fine, but the PR body must name each step and why its blocker is gone.

**A `decision` blocker is never flipped by a machine, and probably not by this step either.** It waits on an answer from Martin. Where the audit finds one whose answer clearly already exists, say so in the PR and let him confirm; where it does not, it stays blocked. The automation this step designs is about *saying* a blocker looks stale, never about deciding it is.

**Then make the next one visible without a person.** Design and build the smallest thing that reports a step blocked on a project that is done: a line in `runner.log` at the end of a round, a row on the page, a line in `mc status` — pick one and say why. Beware of `mc status`'s known trap: it reads the workarea's local checkout, which lags origin/main, so it showed `blocked` for `email-window-layout` step 5 after main already said `ready`. Whatever surface this uses must read the plan on origin/main, which is what the runner obeys.

**What this step does not do.** It does not change what `blocked` means, does not add a status, and does not make the runner start a blocked step. `STEP_STATUSES` stays `ready`/`done`/`blocked` — the fourth status (`waiting-decision`) was deliberately removed and is not coming back.
comments: The sweep, in numbers, from `blocked-scan.mjs` beside the audit. Before: 31 plans on main, 31 blocked steps (29 memoro, 2 memoro-cli), 21 waiting on a `decision` and 10 on a `project`. After: 29 blocked steps, and memoro went from 28 blocked plans against 3 ready to 26 against 5. Two steps were flipped, both waiting on `inbox-finish`, which had been delivered, logged and archived off main the same morning: `home-on-msr` step 2 and `time-axis` step 1, landed as memoro #11280 through `mc merge memoro 11280 --docs`. The goal says 4 ready in memoro and the audit says 3 — `email-window-layout` step 5 was flipped by hand between the two readings, which is the incident this step exists because of.

Twenty-one of the thirty-one waited on a `decision`, and none of them could be resolved here, because **there is no decision file anywhere in either repository** — `git ls-tree -r origin/main | grep decisions/` is empty in both. The `<area>/decisions/` apparatus went with the `waiting-decision` status, so a `decision` blocker is a label with nothing behind it and its answer lives in a plan's prose or in a conversation. Eighteen of the twenty-one are one deliberate park: #11152 converted twenty-six plans in a single commit and blocked every one's next step on `plan-review` by design. It is Martin's reading queue, not a fault, and it is the ceiling on what any automation here can reach — measured on the same refs, only 10 of 31 blocked steps were even machine-checkable.

The finding worth carrying forward, because a later step may want it: **`blocked_by` holds one blocker and a step can be waiting on two things.** `cache-warming` step 3 ("Wait for the audit") and `tool-profiles-per-model` step 1 ("Wait for the numbers") both wait in their instruction on `region-cache-audit`, which was delivered 2026-08-30 and archived by #11143 — but their `blocked_by` says `decision: plan-review`, because the conversion carried one blocker per step and the park took the slot. So the thing they are actually waiting for is finished and nothing can see it, including the mechanism this step built. Two rows did not seem worth a schema change, and it is not this step's to make; it is written down in `blocked-audit.md` § *The second blocker*.

The surface is the page, not `runner.log` and not `mc status`. `mc status <name>` reads the workarea's working tree when there is one (`status-project.js` says so at the top), which is exactly the trap the instruction warned about; `runner.log` is where `run.js` already declines to put plan-shaped refusals, in `refusedLine`'s own words, because they belong on the page. So `queueSection` grew a `stale` key and QUEUE grew a line under `skipped`. The line says **`blocker finished N`** and not *stale*: RUNNER two sections up already spends the word "stale" on a lane file whose process is gone, and one word with two meanings on one page is the kind of thing this repository has guards against.

What the mechanism deliberately will not do. It reads `kind: project` only, never `decision` — see above, there is nothing to check a decision against, and a machine that guessed would be wrong 21 times out of 31. It says *is not on main* rather than *is done*, because a project also leaves main when it is abandoned or superseded (`project_log.md` has both), and then the blocked step's premise may be dead rather than satisfied — only a person can tell which. And it writes nothing: flipping a step back to `ready` stays a plan edit somebody makes and a pull request somebody reads. This step's automation is the noticing, and only that.

For step 2, which measures: `blocked-scan.mjs` takes `--memoro-ref` and `--memoro-cli-ref`, so any past state of the queue can be re-counted from git without a checkout, and `--json` gives the rows. That is also how the before/after table in `blocked-audit.md` was produced.

steps.title: Fewer turns, one test run, a Bash ceiling, visible skips — and each lane on its own clock
steps.done_when: A headless step is launched with `--permission-mode acceptEdits` and a ten-minute Bash ceiling, `canon/roles/step.md` says to read whole files and run the selection once, a dirty-worktree skip names the files, and the unattended `mc run` loop runs one round-loop per repository with the chores beside them — with `measurements.md` and `measure.py` on main as the baseline.
instruction: Done by the planning session on 2026-09-03, in the same PR as this plan: `src/mc/run-plan.js` (`headlessArgs`), `src/mc/run.js` (`realDeps.session` env, the dirty-worktree line, `round({ only })`, `chores()`, the unattended branch of `runLoop`), `canon/roles/step.md`, and this directory's `measure.py` and `measurements.md`.
comments: The two workareas that were skipped every round (`email-window-layout`, `home-on-msr`) had their uncommitted files committed as `wip:` on their branches by hand the same day — nothing was discarded. `inbox-finish` was left: its project is off main and `closeWorkareas` files it as unplanned.

`chores()` archives finished plans only on a pass when no lane is in a session, because an archive lands a docs PR through the gate and the gate still refuses a second round. Once step 3 makes the lock wait, that guard can go.

`--once` and `--rounds N` still drive the old shared round; only the unattended run (`rounds === 0`) has independent lanes. Both are read by the same STOP and UPDATE files, at a lane's round boundary, and the handover waits for every lane.

steps.title: The gate lock queues instead of refusing
steps.done_when: A round that finds the gate lock held waits for it and then takes it, rather than being told no and losing its round — and a test drives two rounds against one lock without either losing work.
instruction: **Keep the guarantee, change the answer.** `gate-lock.js` exists so one gate round runs at a time on this machine — a full suite pins the cores, and two at once make both slower and both flakier, which is the 55 → 57 → 55 the red floor was invented to absorb. That stays exactly as it is. What changes is what happens to the *second* round: today `takeGateLock` returns `{ ok: false, running }` and the caller gives up; the work that round already did is thrown away. With each lane on its own clock (step 1) two landings can now meet more often than they did, and `measurements.md` counted 9 refusals in the history.

**The existing design notes are the constraint, not an obstacle.** `gate-lock.js` deliberately has no expiry, because there is no clock that can tell a slow round from a dead one — a round is *supposed* to take minutes — and the only honest question is whether the pid is alive. A queue must not smuggle a timeout back in through the side door. Waiting on a live pid is correct; waiting forever on a pid that has gone is not, and the existing dead-pid path (`taken, and the pid is gone → take it`) already answers that case.

**Find every caller before changing the contract.** `takeGateLock`'s `{ ok: false, running }` shape is read by callers that report to a person — `running` is *"what to tell the operator, and it is the other round's own words rather than a guess."* A queue changes when that message is useful. Do not remove the ability to say who holds the lock; a round that has been waiting should still be able to say what it is waiting for, and `runner.log` should carry one line when a round waited and for how long.

**`repo-lease.js` is a different guarantee and is not this step.** It is advisory by design and holds one gate round per repository. Say in the PR whether a queued gate round interacts with it, but do not change it here.
**When this lands, `chores()` in `run.js` no longer needs its quiet-pass guard** around `archiveDone` — remove it in the same PR and say so.

steps.title: Measure again, and say whether the count is worth raising
steps.done_when: `measurements.md` § *After* holds the same table as the baseline for at least 20 step sessions started after step 1 landed, and ends with one recommendation: raise the lane count, or not, and why.
instruction: **Measure what exists.** Martin, 2026-09-03: *"20 är bara taget ur luften. Det tar för lång tid allt. Slå på projekten nu."* — so this step runs as soon as step 2 has landed, over every step session started after step 1 landed (2026-09-03 19:35Z). State the session count in the table; a small count is reported as small, not padded.

**Run `measure.py`** with `--since` the day step 1 landed and `--until` today, and paste the output under a `## After` heading in `measurements.md`, beside the baseline. Compare median turns, test-class commands per session, Bash-versus-native calls, the poll/wait share and session wall-clock. State the session count.

**Read `runner.log` for the lanes.** Count `memoro-cli: round N done` lines that fall between a memoro `step starting` and its `step done`; that is the independence step 1 built, and criterion 6 wants a day's worth of it. Count `another gate round is running` in `gate-rounds.jsonl` since the landing; that is the base rate step 4 cares about — step 2 (the queueing lock) lands before this measurement, so count refusals before and after its landing separately.

**End with one recommendation**, written for Martin: whether four lanes in memoro would now buy wall-clock, what it would cost in gate contention, and whether the queueing lock (step 2) has changed the refusal picture. If the honest answer is that the count is still not the bottleneck, say so — the contract says dropping step 4 is a legitimate outcome.

steps.title: The lane count is a setting, and `mc step` is how it is set
steps.done_when: `mc step <n>` sets how many steps may run at once per repository, `mc step` prints the current value, the setting survives a restart, and a round with it above 1 runs several steps in one repository at once without losing work to the gate.
instruction: **Read step 3's recommendation first** — it is in that step's `comments` and in `measurements.md` § *After*. If it says the lane count is not the bottleneck, do not build the count anyway: set this step `blocked` on decision `step-parallelism-count` with the reason, and stop. Otherwise go on; step 2 has made a refused gate a wait, so a wider count no longer throws work away.

**What has to change structurally.** After step 1 the unattended loop in `runLoop` (`src/mc/run.js`) runs one `lane(repo)` loop per repository, each calling `round({ only: repo.name })`, which walks that repository's names serially in `runLane`. A count above one means several steps in flight within one repository's lane; decide the shape and say why in the PR. Note that `runLane` re-reads `queue({ only: repo })` after a merge so a plan advanced by one step is seen by the next — whatever shape is chosen has to keep that true, and two steps in one repository make it harder, not easier.

**Two things a second step in the same repository must not break.** Each step already gets its own workarea and worktree, so the checkouts do not collide. What is shared is the repository's `git fetch` in `queue()` and the `inFlight` rule that stops a project being started while it has an open pull request (`project-prs.js`). Two steps in one repository must not both start the same project, and must not both be mid-`fetch` in the same repository directory.

**Where the setting lives.** `mc` reads its own state under `~/.memoro/mc/` (`src/mc/paths.js`, `mcHome()`), which is where `gate-running.json` and the lease files already are. Follow whatever the nearest existing setting does rather than inventing a new configuration mechanism; if there is no precedent for a persisted user setting, the smallest honest thing is a single JSON file written with `writeJsonAtomic` (`src/mc/atomic-write.js`), the way the gate lock is written.

**The verb.** Martin asked for `mc step` — `mc step 4` sets it, `mc step` with no argument prints it. Keep it to that; a setting with one number does not need subcommands. Check the name against the existing surface first: `mc --help` and the page name the verbs, and `step` is already the word for a *kind* of round in `runs.tsv` and in `chooseKind` (`run-plan.js`). If `mc step` reads as "run a step" to anyone who has seen that vocabulary, say so and propose the name that does not — this is worth one paragraph in the PR, not a redesign.
**Default to today's behaviour.** Whatever the count's default is, an operator who sets nothing must get exactly what they get today. A setting that changes behaviour by existing is not a setting.
**Finish the surface.** `mc --help`, the page, and a technical doc under `docs/technical/` saying what the lane count does and what it costs — including the gate contention the measurements found.
